title: Microsoft Purview: retention for Microsoft 365 Copilot memory
summary: Hold: disabling Enhanced personalization does not preserve all memory; Microsoft says inferred chat-history details are deleted after 30 days. The mixed licensing field also conflicts with the briefing's statement that memory-retention licensing is unpublished. The roadmap facts and the reported disagreement with Learn are supported.

claims.fix: The route stops at the creation wizard. claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published whether those Copilot-interaction licences cover the new memory-retention capability.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Copilot memory retention licensing storage size price memory-specific retention default. Read Purview service description, get-started-with-data-lifecycle-management and Copilot memory page; no memory-retention entitlement.

claims.claim: The memory-retention feature has a mixed licensing model.
claims.quote: model: "mixed"; "Nothing specific to memory retention is published."; "Whether a memory retention capability uses these licences is not yet published."
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'unknown'. Keep the qualified licensing notes about Copilot interactions; the researched sources do not establish entitlement to memory retention.

claims.claim: No separate meter or price for memory retention is published as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot memory retention licensing price meter storage quota; Microsoft 365 Copilot memory retention licensing storage size price memory-specific retention default. Read memory, Purview service description and DLM getting-started pages; no memory price.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published storage figures for Copilot memory.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot memory retention licensing price meter storage quota; Microsoft 365 Copilot memory retention licensing storage size price memory-specific retention default. Read Copilot memory and Purview service description; no memory-storage figures.

claims.claim: Learn places saved memories and inferred chat-history details in a hidden folder in each user's Exchange mailbox.
claims.quote: Memories, which include saved memories, details inferred from chat history and custom instructions, are stored in the user's Exchange mailbox in a hidden folder.

claims.claim: Enhanced personalization is on by default.
claims.quote: Enhanced personalization is the control that allows Copilot memory to be used by end-users. By default, Enhanced personalization is turned on.

claims.claim: Turning Enhanced personalization off stops Copilot applying memory but does not remove memory.
claims.quote: If the Enhanced personalization control is turned off at the admin-level, or if the Chat history control is turned off at the end-user level, then all details from chat history are deleted after 30 days.
claims.fix: Replace 'when it is turned off Copilot stops applying memory but doesn't remove it' with 'when it is turned off Copilot stops applying saved memories but does not remove those saved memories'. This narrows the statement to the Saved memories passage at https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/manage/copilot-personalization-memory.

claims.claim: Admins can search saved and inferred Copilot memories with Purview eDiscovery or Content Search.
claims.quote: Admins can search their users' memory in Microsoft Copilot via Microsoft Purview eDiscovery or Content Search. Custom instructions aren't yet discoverable in these solutions.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The documented item class to search for Copilot memory is IPM.Contact.

claims.claim: Preserved historical memory details would be available to anyone with eDiscovery access.
claims.quote: eDiscovery Managers can only access and manage the cases they create. They can't access or manage cases created by other eDiscovery Managers.
claims.fix: Remove 'available to anyone with eDiscovery access' and write 'Preserving historical versions would retain older inferred details about users, so review who holds eDiscovery roles.' This retains the risk analysis without asserting universal access or an undocumented historical-version retrieval mechanism.
